claim: The model comprises spinal cord, sensory and motor cortex, coupled by long connections that are plastic.
source: In this paper, we show that feedback control is a simple, yet powerful way to understand the neural dynamics of sensorimotor control. We make our case using a minimal model comprising spinal cord, sensory and motor cortex, coupled by long connections that are plastic.
evidence: The abstract directly states the composition of the model.

claim: The model succeeds in learning how to perform reaching movements of a planar arm with 6 muscles in several directions from scratch.

claim: Using differential Hebbian plasticity the model can go from motor babbling to reaching arbitrary targets in less than 10 min of in silico time.

claim: Neural populations in motor cortex show directional tuning as an emergent property of properly configured feedback control.
source: Moreover, independently of the learning mechanism, properly configured feedback control has many emergent properties: neural populations in motor cortex show directional tuning and oscillatory dynamics, the spinal cord creates convergent force fields that add linearly, and movements are ataxic (as in a motor system without a cerebellum).
evidence: The abstract explicitly lists directional tuning as an emergent property.

source: This is because, in mammals, in addition to areas in cortex like premotor and motor areas and to some degree sensory and parietal ones, many extracortical regions have important and unique functions: basal ganglia, thalamus, cerebellum, pons, brain stem nuclei like the red nucleus and spinal cord (Eccles, 1981; Loeb and Tsianos, 2015).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to Eccles, 1981 and Loeb and Tsianos, 2015.

claim: These motor control structures are highly interconnected by fast conducting axons and all show strong dynamic activity changes, related to the ongoing dynamics of the performed motor act.
